newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans hit 4-month lows on weather, exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans hit 4-month lows on weather, exports.

text.p: Favorable growing weather, poor weekly export sales and falling cash soybean values caused July soybeans to fall to four-month lows Thursday and other contracts also ended lower, traders and analysts said.

"There are no worries about the crop right now," said Dale Durchholz, grain analyst with AgriVisor Services in Bloomington, Il. "But you have to be careful getting complacent because we've got a lot of growing season left."
However recent weather in much of the U.S. Midwest has allowed the crop to get off to a healthy start, floor traders said.
On Thursday, USDA reported net export sales for the week ended June 19 for old crop soybeans were 9,200 tonnes. That figure came in far below trade expectations for 50,000 to 100,000 tonnes.
Basis levels in U.S. and Brazilian cash markets have been declining this week, and that weakness was also pressuring futures, traders said.
The falling basis values triggered concerns that China could default on recent soymeal and soybean purchases.
CBOT July soybeans settled down 16-1/4 cents per bushel at $8.00-1/2 cents, and other months were down 7-1/4 to 11-1/4.
July soybeans were being offered at a discount of 40 cents per bushel in Brazil on Wednesday, compared to a 15-cent discount Tuesday.
Fears that a commercial firm is planning heavy deliveries against the July soybean contract on first notice day Monday also pressured futures, traders said.
"The real negative thing today is the deliveries," Durchholtz said.
Traders said that there was talk as many as one million bushels of soybeans were being sent to Chicago for delivery.
Floor traders are looking for quiet trade Friday ahead of the U.S. Department of Agriculture's quarterly stocks report and acreage report on Monday.
On the day, Smith Barney sold 2.5 million bushels November and ADM sold 1.5 million July. Refco bought two million bushels July and Tenco bought 2.5 million July, pit traders said.

In options trade, Refco sold 400 August $8.25 calls and Smith Barney sold 500 September $7.00 calls. Volatility was put at 25 percent in November, 25-1/2 percent in September and 30 percent in September, traders said.
Thursday's volume was estimated at 56,000 contracts. That figure compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 59,616.
